statusText: Tail holds at 20%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. The 31,196.75 session low has now held for a third hour and the 31,196.75-31,466.00 range is unchanged, so price has returned to within about 16 points of the low without setting a new one. A 24-year-high 10-year yield, Brent at 104.43 near its session high and the STOXX 600 at a June low keep Tail at the WATCH floor into the 12:30Z claims print.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 20%, the floor of the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:30Z-16:00Z, spanning the jobless-claims print, the U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 22%. Conditional Tail sits at 19% in the EA_ON band at 11:00Z, returns to that band from 16:00Z, and lifts once more to 20% around the 17:00Z 30-year auction before decaying overnight.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a three-hour base above the session low while a 24-year-high 10-year yield, crude above 104 and a June low in European shares keep conditions difficult
body:
The eleventh Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session has extended a base rather than a new leg down. NQ Dec26 traded 31,212.75 as of 10:16:47Z, -189.50 or -0.60% against a 31,402.25 prior close and a 31,403.00 open, corroborated at 31,214.25 on the same page's index ticker and at 31,208.50 on an independent capture around 10:05Z. The session range is unchanged for a third hour at 31,196.75-31,466.00, worth 269.25 points or 0.86%: no new low and no new high. The 31,196.75 low set in the 07:00Z hour is intact, and price now sits roughly 16 points above it after the 08:20Z recovery to 31,276.50 faded completely. That combination, a failed bounce but a defended low inside an unchanged range, is consolidation rather than the repeated extension after failed retracements that defines a pathological path.

The cross-asset backdrop has, however, kept deteriorating. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.349%, up about 5 basis points, after printing a 24-year high of 5.36% overnight and trading 5.33% in European hours; the 30-year is 5.73% and the 2Y is 4.83%. Reuters reports selling concentrated in French and other heavily indebted euro-area debt, spreading to Italian and Greek bonds and to parts of the banking sector, with the European bank index down close to 2% and the STOXX 600 off about 1% to its lowest since June. The CAC 40 is more than 12% below its August record. Asia closed weaker, with the Nikkei -1.4% and the Kospi -2.6%. The dollar index is near an 18-month peak around 102.34, the euro near a 17-month low at 1.1185, and gold is up 0.6% at about 4,136.

Energy is the second channel. Brent is 104.43, +4.22%, trading near its 104.51 session high on a 100.75-104.51 range, and WTI Nov26 is 91.91, +4.11%, after further attacks on Gulf shipping and around the Strait of Hormuz. A separate report highlights hurricane risk to U.S. refining capacity, which keeps a second, weather-driven supply channel open alongside the geopolitical one. VIX is 15.72, +4.24%, sitting at its 15.74 session high on a 15.31-15.74 range.

Technology fundamentals conflict with the tape, which is the main reason the dominant mode is mixed rather than trend-down. Samsung guided Q3 operating profit to a record 107.4 trillion won, about 80.2 billion dollars and a 782.5% year-on-year jump, ahead of the 106.1 trillion won consensus, on high-bandwidth-memory demand from AI data centres; TSMC September revenue rose 54.6% year on year and its Q3 revenue of about NT$1.49 trillion was a record, above the top of its own guidance. Yet Samsung shares closed 2.42% lower on profit-taking, TSM is -2.09% at 472.20 and NVDA is -0.74% at 237.47, while CAT is -5.75%. Record AI fundamentals are not currently translating into index support.

Policy is the third channel. Fed Governor Waller said in remarks earlier today that more hikes are needed while describing flexibility on the pace, consistent with minutes showing most members expecting another increase by year-end; markets price roughly 19% for this month and about 80% for December. Reported financing plans, including a 50 billion dollar Broadcom package and 30 billion dollars of SpaceX investment-grade debt plus 10 billion in loans for chip purchases, add corporate supply to an already strained duration market.

On the published contract this is a multiple-amplifier environment without the price path that amplifiers would need to matter: yields, oil, the dollar, VIX and global equity breadth are aligned risk-negative, but NQ has produced three hours of unchanged range and a defended low, and it is outperforming the Kospi, Nikkei and STOXX. Tail therefore stays at the 20% WATCH floor rather than advancing toward the 25% blocking threshold, while Stress rises to 62% to carry the difficulty of the environment. Confidence is 88% on fresh corroborated futures quotes, primary-source yields, oil and VIX levels, a verified calendar and verified reporting on the bond, energy and semiconductor channels. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run; its latest publication is dated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness contract and was treated as unavailable, with no influence on these scores.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 14% at the start of the window, rose into a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z on Oct 7 as a trend-down phase developed into the U.S. cash open, then decayed steadily once that cash dip was retraced into the close. Every hour from 16:00Z through 05:00Z held the 10-18% EA_ON band with Stress at 47-53%. The last three lookback hours mark the current episode: Tail lifted to 14% at 06:00Z as the 05:16Z retracement failed, to 22% at 07:00Z once a second failed retracement set the 31,196.75 low, then settled back to 20% at 08:00Z and 09:00Z as that low held and the range stopped expanding. Stress climbed monotonically from 55% to 60% across those same hours as oil and the long end advanced. No past assessment has been altered.
outlookSummary: Base case is that the three-hour base above 31,196.75 resolves into two-way rotation through European and U.S. cash trade, while a 24-year-high 10-year yield, Brent above 104 on both Gulf shipping attacks and U.S. refining weather risk, euro-area spread stress and a confirmed Fed hiking bias remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail eases to 19% in the EA_ON band at 11:00Z, then rises across the 12:30Z claims print to a 22% peak spanning the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour, which is the published 12:30Z-16:00Z danger window. It returns to the EA_ON band at 16:00Z, lifts once to the 20% WATCH floor around the 17:00Z 30-year auction and 17:40Z Musalem remarks given a 5.73% long end, and then decays through the U.S. close to 12-13% across the Asian session before a modest 13-15% allowance into the Oct 9 European hours. Every forecast hour beyond the current one states conditional risk and its invalidation, not observed structure.
